precepts.text: In the Babylonian captivity our fathers still made a collection, according to every man's power, not a set amount.
precepts.point: He which soweth sparingly shall reap sparingly, and he which soweth bountifully shall reap bountifully; that does not mean the Most High blesses you with a three story house, for you may be storing up treasures in heaven. Give as you purpose in your heart, not grudgingly or of necessity, for God loveth a cheerful giver; giving with an attitude is worse than keeping the money.

note.label: Exodus 38: The Altar, the Court, and the Sum of the Offering

precepts.why:
In the wilderness the silver came “A bekah for every man, that is, half a shekel”, from every one numbered from twenty years old and upward, “six hundred thousand and three thousand and five hundred and fifty men.” Thousands of men contributed to the cause of the sanctuary being built. But Israel in the wilderness was delivered, not in captivity.

After Babylon invaded Jerusalem our fathers were captives, yet “they wept, fasted, and prayed before the Lord. They made also a collection of money according to every man’s power”. Not a required amount, but according to every man's power, for the house of the Lord.

Today we are waking up in our captivity, and the buildings we get for sanctuaries require work, wood, service and labor. Likewise the congregations do not push a ten percent; you give according to your power, and the Lord knows how much power you have to give. Sadly some give more than those who have more power to give than they. If you have trouble coming up out of your pocket to help the cause of the Lord, examine yourself whether ye be in the faith, whether you really believe and really study.

precepts.text: Sow bountifully and reap bountifully; give as you purpose in your heart, not grudgingly or of necessity, for God loveth a cheerful giver.
precepts.point: He which soweth sparingly shall reap sparingly, and he which soweth bountifully shall reap bountifully; that does not mean the Most High blesses you with a three story house, for you may be storing up treasures in heaven. Give as you purpose in your heart, not grudgingly or of necessity, for God loveth a cheerful giver; giving with an attitude is worse than keeping the money.

note.label: Exodus 38: The Altar, the Court, and the Sum of the Offering

precepts.why:
“He which soweth sparingly shall reap also sparingly; and he which soweth bountifully shall reap also bountifully.” That does not mean the Most High blesses you with a three story house; you may be storing up treasures in heaven.

“Every man according as he purposeth in his heart, so let him give; not grudgingly, or of necessity: for God loveth a cheerful giver.” As in the wilderness, when thousands of men gave their half shekels for the sanctuary, and as in Babylon, when our fathers made a collection according to every man's power, you give according to your power and as you purpose in your heart. Giving with an attitude is worse than keeping the money. Many do not have the spirit to give; if you have trouble coming up out of your pocket for the cause of the Lord, examine yourself whether ye be in the faith.

precepts.text: The bountiful reaping may be treasures laid up in heaven rather than riches in this life.

Give as you purpose in your heart, not grudgingly or of necessity, for God loveth a cheerful giver; giving with an attitude is worse than keeping the money.

note.label: Exodus 38: The Altar, the Court, and the Sum of the Offering

precepts.why:
“But lay up for yourselves treasures in heaven, where neither moth nor rust doth corrupt, and where thieves do not break through nor steal”.

He which soweth bountifully shall reap bountifully, but the reaping is not necessarily a three story house in this life. The bountiful reaping may be treasures laid up in heaven rather than riches here. That is what the thousands of men gave toward with their half shekels for the sanctuary, and what a cheerful giver gives toward today.

points: This chapter is the application of the instructions already given for the tabernacle: the altar of burnt offering of shittim wood overlaid with brass, its vessels, and its staves were made exactly as commanded.

note.label: Exodus 38: The Altar, the Court, and the Sum of the Offering

points: The laver of brass was made of the looking glasses of the women assembling at the door of the tabernacle of the congregation; even the women's own possessions went into the work.

note.label: Exodus 38: The Altar, the Court, and the Sum of the Offering

points: This is the sum of the tabernacle: a collection was taken in order to fund the building of the tabernacle and the service of building it, counted according to the commandment of Moses by the hand of Ithamar son to Aaron the priest.

note.label: Exodus 38: The Altar, the Court, and the Sum of the Offering

points: All the gold, silver, and brass occupied for the work was counted. The silver came a bekah for every man, half a shekel after the shekel of the sanctuary, from every one numbered from twenty years old and upward, six hundred thousand and three thousand and five hundred and fifty men. Thousands of men contributed to the cause of the sanctuary being built.

After Babylon invaded Jerusalem our fathers were captives, yet they still made a collection for the house of the Lord, not a required amount but according to every man's power. Likewise today the congregations do not push a ten percent; you give according to your power, and the Lord knows how much power you have to give. Sadly some give more than those who have more power to give than they.

note.label: Exodus 38: The Altar, the Court, and the Sum of the Offering

points: The brass of the offering, seventy talents and two thousand and four hundred shekels, made the sockets of the door, the brasen altar and its grate and vessels, the sockets of the court, and all the pins of the tabernacle and the court. Every material was accounted for; not everybody had the spirit to contribute physically, but everybody put their brick in and gave something for the cause.
